newsitem.title: CZECH REPUBLIC: Blue chip losses pull Czech PSE index lower.
newsitem.headline: Blue chip losses pull Czech PSE index lower.

text.p: The Prague Stock Exchange's PX50 index lost ground on Thursday as the three most heavily capitalised shares -- which account for 45 percent of total index capitalisation -- all posted losses.
SPT Telecom led the way with a 61 crown fall to 4,329, while CEZ dropped five crowns to 943 and Komercni Banka lost 58 crowns to 1,987.
Total volume, boosted mainly by direct and block trades, was heavier at 1.22 million shares on turnover of 1.5 billion crowns. Overall, 127 shares closed higher, 63 were lower and 41 held steady.

Radio transmission company Ceske Radiokomunikace continued to surge, jumping the maximum daily allowed five percent to hit 4,400. TeleDanmark said on Tuesday it had taken a 21 percent stake in the Czech company.
Analysts and dealers said that the TeleDanmark purchase was good news for Radiokomunikace's long term prospects but noted that very few shares now remained on the open market.
The state owns 70 percent of Radiokomunikace's shares.
